questions.q: Do French adverbs agree with anything?
questions.why: An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb, and never changes form. Only adjectives agree.

questions.q: Place the adverb: build « I often eat here. »
questions.why: In a simple tense the adverb comes after the verb. French never puts it between subject and verb, so « je souvent mange » is impossible.

questions.q: Place the adverb: build « I have already eaten. »
questions.why: Short adverbs (bien, mal, déjà, encore, toujours, souvent, trop, beaucoup, presque) sit between the auxiliary and the past participle.

questions.q: Where does a long adverb like « immédiatement » go in a compound tense?
choices: Between the auxiliary and the participle
questions.why: Only short adverbs squeeze inside: « J'ai bien mangé » but « J'ai répondu immédiatement. »

questions.q: Complete: Je vais à la piscine deux fois ___ semaine.
questions.why: The rate pattern is always __ fois par __ : une fois par jour, trois fois par semaine, deux fois par an. Never dans or à.

questions.q: Say this frequency expression out loud.
questions.why: De temps en temps means from time to time. It is four words but one unit, said without a break.
Bien is the adverb and modifies the verb. Bon is the adjective and modifies a noun: « C'est un bon chanteur. »

questions.q: « Actuellement, je travaille à Paris. » What does actuellement mean?
questions.why: Actuellement means currently. For actually, say en fait. Its partner false friend is éventuellement, which means possibly, not eventually (that is finalement).

questions.q: Which connector opens the sentence? ___ il pleut, on reste ici. (since / as)
questions.why: Comme can only start a sentence. Car does the opposite: it never starts one. Parce que is the general-purpose everyday choice.

choices: grâce à = negative outcome, à cause de = positive outcome
grâce à = positive outcome, à cause de = negative outcome
grâce à takes a verb, à cause de takes a noun
questions.why: « Grâce à toi, j'ai réussi » is a thank-you; « À cause de la grève, je suis en retard » is a complaint. En raison de is the neutral formal option.

questions.q: Contrast connector: Il est fatigué, ___ il travaille. (however)
questions.why: Pourtant and cependant both mean however or yet. Quand même adds the sense of anyway or in spite of it all.

questions.q: Which of these takes the subjunctive?
questions.why: « Bien qu'il soit fatigué » takes the subjunctive; « Même s'il est fatigué » takes the indicative. They mean nearly the same thing, so même si is the safe option.

questions.q: « Il pleut, ___ on ne sort pas. » Which fits, in everyday speech?
questions.why: Du coup marks a consequence and is everywhere in spoken French; donc is the neutral written equivalent. Pourtant would reverse the logic.
Presque jamais means almost never, and presque slots in front of the jamais it modifies.

questions.q: Name the four connectors the chapter says make you sound native, with their meanings.
a: du coup (so, as a result), en fait (actually), quand même (still, anyway), d'ailleurs (besides, incidentally)
questions.why: All four are constant in spoken French and nearly absent from textbooks, so using them changes how you sound more than extra vocabulary does.

questions.q: Build the sentence: He answered immediately.
questions.why: A long adverb goes after the participle. A short one goes between auxiliary and participle: j'ai bien dormi.
